# `sesam clean --aggressive` must find the sesam dir like every other command:
# walk up from the cwd (or --sesam-dir) to the nearest `.sesam/`. Run from a
# subdirectory of a nested sesam dir it has to clean the whole sesam tree
# instead of failing with "not a sesam directory".

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

mkdir vault
exec sesam init --user admin --sesam-dir vault
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

mkdir vault/sub
cp leaked vault/sub/leaked.txt
cp leaked vault/leaked.txt

# The soft clean resolves upward from vault/sub...
cd vault/sub
exec sesam clean --dry-run
stdout 'README\.md'

# ...and so must the aggressive one. It lists the untracked files of the whole
# sesam dir (paths are sesam-relative, as for the soft clean) instead of erroring.
exec sesam clean --aggressive --dry-run
stdout 'sub/leaked\.txt'
stdout '^leaked\.txt$'
exists leaked.txt
exists ../leaked.txt

exec sesam clean --aggressive --quiet
! exists leaked.txt
! exists ../leaked.txt
# Tracked files of the sesam dir survive.
exists ../sesam.yml
exists ../.gitignore

-- leaked --
leaked plaintext
